Preprint (arXiv)
Independent Researcher (KC); University of Tennessee, Knoxville (Budathoki)

Compares (four handoff views for a successor agent resuming interrupted work, holding the checkpointed repository fixed); secondary: proposes an evaluation method (takeover protocol / handoff-point benchmark built from SWE-bench Verified, and a structured handoff schema)

No SDD tool. Four handoff views (no versions): (1) Repository only (baseline: checkpointed repo + original task prompt); (2) Raw trace (predecessor event log up to the checkpoint); (3) Summary notes (free-form natural-language notes generated by the predecessor-side model); (4) Structured notes (authors' fixed-field 'bounded continuation contract')

Structured handoff note with deterministic fields (repository change state, changed source files, non-source artifacts, validation outcome after latest source change, latest validation command, latest validation evidence, continuation-state label) and model-generated fields (problem understanding, work completed, evidence observed, observed failures, remaining uncertainty, rollback notes, recommended next action). Summary notes: free text (investigation, edits, validation attempts, uncertainty, next steps). Raw trace: event history

Predecessor agent (Qwen) works on a SWE-bench task -> interrupted at a deterministic handoff point (after first source edit / after first validation result / after first post-failure edit) -> repository frozen -> handoff view generated (notes by predecessor-side model, temperature 0, 1,600-token cap) -> successor agent takes over with the view + original prompt -> official SWE-bench validation

Agent = OpenHands-style runtime (native tool calling disabled; 4 h timeout, 500 steps) for all; predecessor Qwen3.6-27B. Criterion: official SWE-bench resolution; cost = median agent events and prompt tokens. Values: solved rate; median events; median prompt tokens (Table 2). Robustness (Qwen->Qwen, 40 points x 3 repeats, events/tokens only): repo only 102.5 events, 1.62M; raw trace 42 (-59%), 906k; summary 52 (-49%), 591k; structured 58 (-43%), 677k (Table 4). Predecessor robustness (Devstral successor): Gemma and Devstral predecessors also show 21-46% event reductions (Table 6)

Tasks: 75 SWE-bench Verified source tasks (seed 20260430) -> 181 handoff points. Configurations: 4 handoff views x 3 successor models (Qwen, Gemma, Devstral), predecessor fixed to Qwen. Baseline: repository only. Held constant: predecessor, handoff point, checkpointed repository, successor model, runtime, takeover instruction block, serving configuration. Acceptance tests: official SWE-bench held-out tests. Repetitions: 1 per handoff point and view in main study; robustness subset 3 repeats; second robustness with 3 predecessors (6,120 runs). Human intervention: none

Cost: all context-bearing views cut median agent events (raw trace -57 to -59%, notes -20 to -46%) and prompt tokens (-42 to -63%) vs repository only; all matched bootstrap CIs below zero. Quality: raw trace +6.1 to +14.9 pp (significant for all three successors); notes +1.1 to +5.0 pp for Qwen and Gemma (not significant), +9.4/+10.5 pp for Devstral (significant). No single best view across successors; summary vs structured notes similar. Raw trace first prompt median 87k chars vs 7.2k (repo), 9.8k (summary), 10.0k (structured). Largest gains at 'after first post-failure edit' (+12.9 pp Qwen, +19.4 pp Devstral). Small negative deltas for Gemma note views in 'needs completion' state. No multiple-comparison correction

Distinguished views clearly on cost (events, tokens), less on solved rate (model-dependent, often n.s.). Repeatability: robustness rerun (3 attempts, 40 points) and predecessor-robustness study reproduce the efficiency pattern. Limitations stated: one runtime (OpenHands-style); single run per handoff point in main study; 75 source tasks; SWE-bench validation does not cover maintainability or human usefulness; no multiple-comparison correction

Conclusions limited to one OpenHands-style runtime (absolute counts may change elsewhere); single-run handoffs in main study; 75 source tasks; validation covers patch correctness only, not maintainability or human usefulness. Gaps: benchmarks should report handoff debt alongside resolution; agent systems should make handoff output a deliberate part of the workflow; protocol could evaluate adaptive memory policies

Code public: github.com/anjilab/agent-handoff-debt. No pre-registration. Language: Python (SWE-bench). Open-weight models served locally via vLLM on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs; model identifiers Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B, google/gemma-4-31B-it, mistralai/Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct-2512.
